repo_prior_art.cite: none; closest active experimentation proposals concern pilot design or mixed-design degree frontiers, not semilinear versus unrestricted off-policy selector risk.

published_prior_art.cite: ChenValiantValiant2020 poses the semilinear-versus-unrestricted gap for generic sample-target laws; DonohoLiuMacGibbon1990 gives a Gaussian quadratically-convex comparison, not this selector experiment.

ChenValiantValiant2020, Fact 1 and Section 1.3, establishes strict separation and identifies the unrestricted-gap question rather than proving a constant comparison on product-Bernoulli Fourier selectors.

HarshawSavjeWang2022 gives consistency conditions for its Riesz-estimator class; LoombaEckles2026OffPolicy supplies a sufficient spectral-overlap variance condition for its transported estimator, not an all-procedure iff frontier.

WainwrightJordan2004 establishes treewidth-based exactness conditions for polynomial-system relaxation hierarchies, not localization of assignment-indexed minimax weights and global-target epigraph state.
LoombaEckles2026OffPolicy Theorem 5.1 gives the maximum-overlap sufficient envelope; it does not provide a growing additive-hub family with an all-estimator n^{-1} minimax characterization.
CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023 supplies Bernoulli low-order-interference estimation and a minimax lower-bound technique; the stated bounded-prior tensorization is a supporting specialization.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives a π/2 approximation to optimal semilinear mean estimation, exhibits a strict semilinear-versus-unconstrained gap, and explicitly asks about the size of that gap.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3–4, equations (2), (6), and (8); pp. 7–8, Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses biased Fourier transport under heterogeneous product Bernoulli assignment and gives the variance envelope B(n)(D(n)+1)/n, hence a sufficient consistency condition for its transported estimator.
The alpha-non-expanding condition yields a constant lower bound for every estimator, rather than an instance-specific comparison throughout a vanishing-risk selector class.
The 1.25 linear-to-all-estimator comparison is for Gaussian shift models over orthosymmetric quadratically convex sets; the paper also notes arbitrarily large nonlinear gains outside that geometry.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 10–12, Definition 2 and Proposition 2.2; p. 4, Corollary 1.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper represents its unrestricted contrastive-effect minimax risk through an estimand-specific conflict graph and provides GATE bounds through the two-hop graph.
The paper studies TTE under Bernoulli assignment with low-order neighborhood interactions, giving an unbiased estimator, variance analysis, a minimax lower bound, and asymptotic normality.
The report gives sufficient treewidth-based conditions for exactness of Sherali-Adams and Lasserre relaxations for polynomial systems, not the proposed raw-incidence optimizer-localization theorem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Introduce an explicit fixed-instance class parallel to Adm, then quantify the universal, prior-rounding, and treewidth claims over that named class rather than the informal phrase “admissible instance.”

Make the prior-rounding OEQ attackable with a smallest nontrivial selector instance and a stated posterior-ambiguity invariant that the rounding must preserve; use exhaustive finite-instance search as a falsification screen before attempting the universal theorem.
Strengthen the hub result into a fully explicit comparison theorem giving the Loomba–Eckles envelope’s asymptotic order and the frontier constants for a fixed p,q regime, not only Θ/Ω notation.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 on the universal genuine-prior rounding kernel, with explicit small-instance counterexample search and a fixed-instance quantifier definition.
